info.desc: Is This It is the debut album by the American alternative rock band The Strokes, released in 2001. The Strokes were the first band to break into the mainstream as part of the turn-of-the-millennium garage rock revival trend. Hyped by the music press for their melodic pop-influenced garage rock sound on both sides of the Atlantic, The Strokes' auspicious debut garnered them critical and popular attention. Moreover, Is This It's more famous songs "The Modern Age", "Last Nite", "Hard to Explain" and "Someday" won the band much respect and helped the album reach number two in the United Kingdom and .

podcast.body: For their debut album, The Strokes intentionally processed their professional studio recordings by passing them through the electromagnetic spectrum of a cassette tape. This technique was employed to deliberately degrade the sound quality, aiming to emulate the distinctive "cut" and "scratched" sound characteristic of punk and 1980s rock music that was often heard on cassette tapes. "uno de los procesos que hicieron para ese sonido tan característico que tiene el primer disco de los Strokes, fue pasar toda la grabación de los formatos profesionales a un espectro electromagnético de la cinta de cassette para luego hacer la grabación final."

podcast.body: The Strokes' 2001 debut album featured dual cover art designs. The North American version prominently displayed a scientific photograph of subatomic particles in a bubble chamber, while international releases depicted a provocative shot of a woman's naked rear and hip adorned with a black glove, photographed by Colin Lane. The band ultimately preferred the scientific image for global release, but it was too late for the initial pressings. "If you bought the record in North America, we see something very scientific."

"The result was an album called This Is It."

podcast.title: Debut Album
podcast.body: The Strokes' debut album was recorded after Gil Norton was replaced by Gordon Raphael, taking about six weeks in a "crappy studio" that nevertheless had its charms. Guitar teacher JP Bauerstock was brought in to help with guitar lessons, influencing the album's solos. Most tracks were recorded once to maintain rawness, a technique supported by their extensive rehearsal to a click track. This raw approach initially concerned RCA, their US label, who found it unprofessional. The band used only three microphones for a gritty sound, and Julian sang his vocals through a tiny practice amp for a low-fi effect. RCA only understood the vision after hearing the songs played on an old boombox. The album was released in Australia in July 2001, the UK in August, and North America in October. It sold over 4 million copies worldwide and significantly influenced many subsequent bands, including Kings of Leon and The Killers. "The whole thing was recorded using just three microphones to get that gritty raw sound."
